description:
FILED s449/s450 (Fable, round-8 review of agent U) from an own probe.  PRE-EXISTING -- identical on pre-#477 main (eager $&) and after (lazy offsets); nothing to do with U-s change, which only made the reviewer look.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    "zq" =~ /(z)/;
    $_ = "p1 p2 p3";
    while (/(p\d)/g) { }          # three successful matches inside
    print "one=[$1] amp=[$&]\n";
        perl: one=[z] amp=[z]     -- the PRE-loop match is RESTORED at block exit
        PCL:  one=[p3] amp=[p3]   -- last successful match, kept globally

perlre: the match variables are "dynamically scoped until the end of the enclosing block or until the next successful match".  PCL implements the second half (a FAILED match keeps the previous values -- probed, correct) and specific frames (sort comparators), but not the general block-exit restore.  ir-spec SS8-s "dynamically saved/restored around scopes like Perl" overstates what is implemented -- fix the doc or the runtime together.

COST OF FIXING: a save/restore of the whole match state around EVERY block is a hot-path price (the #477 lesson: offsets are cheap to save, memos/subject pointers too -- the state is now 6 slots + the capture group array, so a block save is O(groups), not O(subject)).  Measure which suite rows sit behind it before building; the while-//g-then-read idiom is the common spelling.

BAR: the repro + the failed-match inverse + a sort-comparator frame check vs perl; the op/+re/ companion legs (cl/ change); Target-A guard that the m//g loop timing curve stays linear.

=== s543t (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28) === #932's SUB half is done (p-sub-frame's %p-match-scope, docs/ir-spec.md "Match variables"); this task's BLOCK half is unchanged and re-probed: `{ "bb" =~ /(b)/; } print $1` perl the outer value (or undef), PCL b; `if ("st" =~ /(s)(t)/) { eval { "zz" =~ /(z)/; die "x\n" }; print $1 }` perl s, PCL z.  The machinery to reuse: %p-match-scope is a macro over any body -- a block scope would wrap the block's body the same way, gated by the emitter on "the block contains a match op" (the cost is a special binding per block entry, which a loop body pays per iteration: measure first).

=== s543t (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28): FOUR BOARD ROWS NOW KEYED HERE ===
URI-5.34-0 t/generic.t rows 25 29 39 40 (baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv, re-keyed from #932 by s543t, whose sub-frame scope fixed five rows of the same file): URI::_generic::authority / query match the URI, then -- inside `if (@_) { ... if (defined $auth) { ... } }` -- run s///e and a list-context match of their own, and return `$2` at the sub's end; perl restores the captures at each block's exit, PCL does not.  Neutral reproducer (perl h:8, PCL `:`):
    sub a { "x//h:8/p" =~ m,^(x)(?://([^/]*))?(.*)$, or die; if (@_) { my $v = shift; if (defined $v) { $v =~ s/(h)/H/; my ($u) = $v =~ /^(.)(.)/; } } $2 }
    print a("h:9"), "\n";
  The same matches at the sub's own level (no block) leave perl's $2 the inner match's (undef) -- so it is the BLOCK, not the sub.  Frequency: ordinary (URI is a board dist).

=== s543t review (the reviewing session's probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1128/rt/p/t-01.pl rows 9-11, perl -> main 655db409 -> the s543t tree 82221cf8) ===
Three residues of the capture scope, ONE missing piece: a scope that is not a sub frame, and a non-local exit through a sub frame.  Since s543t a SUB is a scope (p-sub-frame's %p-match-scope, restored at the NORMAL exit only); these are not:
    my @l = map { /(\d)/; $1 } qw(a1 b2); print "9 @l [", (defined $1 ? $1 : "u"), "]\n";        # after `"x" =~ /(x)/` earlier in the file: perl 9 1 2 [x]   base [2]   tree [2]   (a map BLOCK)
    sub viaeval { eval { "ee" =~ /(e)/; die "x\n" }; defined $1 ? $1 : "u" } "T" =~ /(T)/; my $ve = viaeval(); print "10 $ve [$1]\n";   # perl 10 T [T]   base e [e]   tree e [T]   (an eval BLOCK inside the sub)
    sub dies { "dd" =~ /(d)/; die "boom\n" } "K" =~ /(K)/; eval { dies() }; print "11 [$1]\n";   # perl 11 [K]   base [d]   tree [d]   (a DIE through the sub frame: the restore runs on the normal exit only)
The block half: wrap a block body (map / grep / sort blocks, eval BLOCK, bare and loop blocks) in the same macro, gated by the emitter on "the block contains a match op" (the s543t #5545 design note: one walk, no new scope walk); the die half: the restore under an unwind-protect, or the catcher (p-eval-block / p-try) restoring the snapshot of the frames it unwinds -- measure the per-call cost first (#5545's numbers).
subject: Match variables are BLOCK-scoped in perl -- leaving the enclosing block RESTORES $&/$1/../%+ to the pre-block match; PCL keeps last-successful globally (visible after every while-//g loop)
triage_reason: match variables are block-scoped in perl (one family with #932)
